main_answer_reason: The report substantially reconstructs the mortgage transactions, contested eligibility, tax evidence, 1943 findings, High Court reasoning and accounting objection's procedural history. It correctly withholds the ultimate disposition and recognizes uncertainty about raising the accounting objection on further appeal. However, it omits section 8(3)'s limitation on reconsidering decree findings, the operative sections 9–10 recalculation framework, and the distinct unresolved characterization of the 1931 transaction. Its description of the original pleading silence as a concession overstates the available record. These omissions prevent a fully supported treatment of the substantive statutory accounting question.
